title: In Vitro Selection of Aptamers to Differentiate Infectious from Non-Infectious Viruses
protocol: Add 0.9 M Tris-base, 0.9 M boric acid, and 20 mM EDTA (disodium salt) to deionized water to make 1 L of 10x TBE buffer.
Mix all components until dissolved in the 10x TBE preparation.
Add 120 g of urea (8 M), 25 mL of 10x TBE, 62.5 mL of 40% acrylamide/bisacrylamide solution to a final volume of 250 ml with distilled water for the denaturing polyacrylamide stock solution.
Mix all components until dissolved in the denaturing polyacrylamide stock preparation.
Add 21.636 g of urea (8 M), 1.675 g of EDTA, and 4.5 mL of 10x TBE to distilled water for a final volume of 45 ml for the loading buffer.
Mix all components until dissolved in the loading buffer preparation.
Prepare extraction buffer by adding 100 mM sodium acetate and 1 mM EDTA (disodium salt) and setting the pH to 5.0.
Prepare 3 M sodium acetate solution, adjust pH to 5.2, and store at 4°C.
Prepare 70% ethanol, v/v, and store at -20°C.
Prepare 100% ethanol and store at -20°C.
Prepare 500 mL of SELEX buffer containing 1x PBS, 2.5 mM MgCl2, and 0.5 mM CaCl2. Adjust to pH 7.4.
Prepare 100 mL of SELEX buffer with 8 M urea by adding 1x PBS, 2.5 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM CaCl2, and 8 M urea. Adjust to pH 7.4.
In a 50 mL tube, prepare 5 mM Tris, 0.5 mM EDTA (disodium salt), and 2 M NaCl. Adjust to pH 7.5.
Design the initial ssDNA library with a central random region of 35 to 60 nucleotides flanked by two constant sequences at the 3' and 5' ends for amplification.
Ensure the reverse primer contains a biotin modification for separation using streptavidin-coated beads during in vitro selection.
Purchase DNA oligos from commercial sources with standard desalting purification.
Purify ssDNA library and primers by 10% denaturing polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (dPAGE) according to standard procedures.
Precipitate purified ssDNA using ethanol according to standard procedures.
Resuspend ssDNA in nuclease-free water up to a desired concentration of 100 μM.
Determine the concentration of ssDNA library and primers by UV absorption at λ = 260 nm.
Store ssDNA at -20°C.
Purchase an unmodified reverse primer for high-throughput sequencing library preparation and qPCR quantification.
Handle infectious and non-infectious virus samples in a biosafety cabinet or sealed container due to their BSL2 classification.
Prepare stock solutions of infectious viruses or pseudoviruses as per the provided protocol.
Obtain SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV-1, and H5N1 pseudoviruses in PBS buffer from Prof. Lijun Rong's lab (UIC).
For biosafety level 3 required viruses, use pseudotyped viruses generated from lentivirus displaying the virus surface proteins.
Obtain UV-inactivated SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus stock solution in PBS buffer from Prof. Rong's lab.
Prepare UV-inactivated SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus using the reported protocol.
Test the infectivity of the virus to ensure complete inactivation.
Quantify infectious viruses or pseudoviruses using a plaque assay according to standard procedures.
Quantify the virus using a commercially available quantitative lentivirus ELISA kit.
Prepare 1 x 10^8 copies/mL of stock solution for p-SARS-CoV-2, p-SARS-CoV-1, and p-H5N1.
Separate each stock solution in aliquots containing 50 µL each and store at -80 °C.
Thaw a new aliquot before each experiment.
Denature the ssDNA library.
Take 10 µL of 100 µM of the ssDNA library (1 nmol) and mix with 240 µL of SELEX buffer.
Heat the mixture at 95 °C for 15 min in a dry bath, then place the tube on ice for 15 min.
Incubate the ssDNA library with the infectious virus (positive selection step).
Mix 250 µL of ssDNA library in SELEX buffer from step 4.1 with 50 µL of infectious virus (1 x 10^8 copies/mL).
Incubate for 2 h at room temperature.
Block nonspecific sites in centrifuge filters.
While waiting on step 4.2, prepare the centrifuge filters for the next steps.
Add 400 µL of 1 mM T20 sequence to each 0.5 mL centrifuge filter with a cut-off of 100 kDa and one with a cut-off of 10 kDa.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature and centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 10 min to remove the T20 solution in the filter.
Wash 3 times with SELEX buffer to remove excess T20 sequences.
Add the mix incubated in step 4.2 to the blocked 100 kDa centrifuge filter and centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 10 min.
Discard the flow-through and retain the fraction in the filter.
Wash unbound sequences by adding 400 µL of SELEX buffer and centrifuging at 14,000 x g for 10 min, repeating this process 3 times.
Change the collection tube of the centrifuge filter and add 300 µL of SELEX buffer containing 8 M urea to the centrifuge filter in step 4.4.
Heat the centrifuge filter at 95 °C for 15 min in a dry bath.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 10 min and collect the fraction that flowed through the filter containing the eluted sequences.
Repeat this elution process another three times.
Concentrate and desalt by adding the solution collected in 4.5 to a blocked 10 kDa centrifuge filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 15 min and discard the fraction that flowed through the filter.
Wash the filter 3 times with 300 μL of SELEX buffer to remove urea by centrifuging at 14,000 x g for 15 min.
Discard the fraction that flowed through the filter after washing.
Recover the solution in the filter by turning it upside down in a clean collection tube and centrifuging for 5 min.
Measure the final volume of the recovered solution using a pipette in a plastic tube.
Take 1 μL of the eluted ssDNA to quantify the amount of DNA by qPCR.
Perform PCR amplification with a 50 µL reaction mixture containing 1x PCR buffer, 200 µM dNTPs, 10 µL of DNA template (R1a sample), 200 nM each primer, and 1.25 U polymerase (2.5 U/µL stock).
Optimize PCR conditions including number of cycles and annealing temperature for each set of primers and ssDNA library.
Avoid using too many cycles to prevent undesired PCR subproducts such as primer-dimers.
Test different annealing temperatures based on the melting temperature of the primers.
Run PCR using optimized conditions at 95 °C for 5 min followed by 18 cycles of 1 min at 95 °C, 30 s at 52 °C, and 1 min at 72 °C.
Include a final extension step at 72 °C for 10 min to obtain the dsDNA pool.
Take 80% of the PCR product.
Store the remaining fraction at -20 °C.
Split the PCR product into aliquots of 50 µL and add them to microfuge tubes containing 50 µL of streptavidin-modified magnetic beads (MB).
Incubate for 30 min with mild agitation at room temperature.
Place the microfuge tube on the magnetic rack to isolate the MB.
Remove the supernatant by pipetting, ensuring it is a clear solution.
Wash by adding 200 µL of binding and washing buffer to the tube.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack, tap the tube, and resuspend the MB to a homogeneous solution by pipetting.
Place the microfuge tube back on the magnetic rack to isolate the MB.
Remove the supernatant by pipetting.
Repeat this washing step twice.
Resuspend MB in 100 µL of SELEX buffer after washing is complete.
Heat the solution to 95 °C for 10 min.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack before it cools down.
Take the supernatant containing the ssDNA pool.
Repeat the recovery step, adding 50 µL of SELEX buffer.
Measure the final volume of the recovered fraction using a pipette.
Denature the ssDNA pool from sample R1x by heating at 95 °C for 15 min in a dry bath.
Place the tube on ice for 15 min after heating.
Incubate the denatured ssDNA pool with non-infectious virus and other potential interfering viruses for 1 h at room temperature.
Block nonspecific sites in centrifuge filters using two centrifuge filters, one with a cut-off of 100 kDa and one with a cut-off of 10 kDa.
Wash away sequences bound to non-target viruses.
Add the mix incubated in step 5.2 to a blocked 100 kDa centrifuge filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 10 min and recover the fraction that flows through the centrifuge filter.
Wash two times, adding 100 µL of SELEX buffer and centrifuging at 14,000 x g for 10 min.
Incubate the ssDNA pool with the infectious virus (positive selection step).
Mix 300 µL of fraction from step 5.4 with 50 µL of the infectious virus (1 x 108 copies/mL).
Incubate for 2 h at room temperature.
Prepare a standard qPCR mixture containing 5 µL of master mix, 0.3 µL of 500 nM of each unlabeled primer, 3.4 µL of H2O, and 1 µL of DNA template.
Dilute the purified ssDNA library to fit within the concentration range of the standard curve.
Add 1 µL of sample without dilution and 1 µL of a 1:10 dilution to the qPCR mixture for Ria samples.
Include 1:10 or 1:100 dilutions in the qPCR mixture for Rix samples.
Set an initial denaturation step at 98 °C for 2 min.
Set 40 cycles of denaturation at 98 °C for 5 s and annealing and extension at 52 °C for 10 s.
Set a melting curve analysis from 65 to 95 °C.
Determine threshold cycle (Ct) values by automated threshold analysis.
Quantify the amount of ssDNA in Ria and Rix samples using the standard curve.
Calculate the elution yield as the amount of bound DNA divided by the amount of initial DNA.
Plot the elution yield vs round number to observe enrichment over rounds.
Plot melting curves for different rounds.
Consult with the high-throughput sequencing facility about available sequencing types and scales.
Determine library preparation method based on pool length and number of pools.
Select an appropriate commercially available kit based on the type of sequencing in consultation with the sequencing facility.
Prepare multiple pools of selection rounds representing high, medium, and low enrichment using different indexes for each pool.
Perform end repair of fragmented DNA as part of library preparation.
Ligate adaptors to the repaired DNA fragments.
Amplify the ligated products via PCR.
Purify the amplified PCR product with magnetic DNA clean-up beads following manufacturer's instructions.
Quantify the purified DNA using a fluorescence-based quantification kit.
Mix approximately equal amounts of each pool library containing specific indexes by DNA amount, not volume.
Check the quality of the final library with qPCR quantification.
Analyze the fragment size distribution of the final library with a DNA fragment analyzer.
Discuss library preparation and quality control procedures with sequencing facility personnel.
Send the prepared final library to the sequencing facility following their requirements.
Access the sequencing files, usually in a compressed FastQ file format, using the information provided by the sequencing facility.
Use an FTP client to transfer files to your computer and/or high-performance computing resource.
Keep files compressed if possible to limit their file sizes.
Uncompress sequence files using gzip if needed.
Clean up sequences before analysis by demultiplexing.
Remove sequencing adapters from the sequences.
Remove low quality reads from the sequences.
Include both forward- and reverse-direction reads in the analysis.
Use FastQC program after each clean-up step for basic quality control information.
Use Cutadapt to remove sequencing adapters using the command-line program.
Set the --discard-untrimmed option to discard sequences without selection primers.
Input selection primers in Linked Adapter mode instead of sequencing adapters.
Configure options for maximum error rate matching the adapters.
Specify minimum and maximum length thresholds for accepted sequences.
If using paired-end reads, provide Read 1 and Read 2 files as inputs.
Run Cutadapt a second time with reverse-complement of selection primers (optional).
Merge Read 1 and Read 2 files using PEAR if paired-end sequencing is employed (optional).
Use the FASTX-Toolkit program to remove low-quality sequences with a quality score below 30.
If overall quality is good, skip this step.
Use the fastx_reverse_complement function in FASTX-Toolkit on reverse direction files.
Merge forward and reverse-complement-reverse files into a single file using the cat program.
Analyze sequence enrichment across different selection pools using FASTAptamer analysis toolkit.
Count the number of times each sequence appears with FASTAptamer-Count.
Rank and sort sequences by abundance.
Use the count output file as input for all other FASTAptamer programs.
Group all sequences into clusters using FASTAptamer-Clust.
Define the number of single nucleotide mutations or indels allowed to group into a cluster using the "distance" parameter.
Perform initial screening of candidate aptamers using a column-based ultrafiltration binding assay or ELONA for multiple samples quickly.
Analyze the specificity and affinity of sequences showing best binding activity from initial screening.
Use at least two independent binding assays such as MicroScale Thermophoresis, Enzyme-Linked Oligonucleotide Assay, surface plasmon resonance, or biolayer interferometry.
